statusDetail: Atomic audit completed across home, section, article, and search journey. Search returned a directly observed 403 failure state.

page.notes: Server-rendered German news portal with large MPA-style route surface, consent wall, third-party widgets, and external search endpoint. Coverage excludes authenticated email/account management, paid PUR checkout, video playback, games, and regional subdomains because they are separate products or gated flows; one representative page per core editorial archetype was selected.

principleOutcomes.reason: All checks were judged contextually out of scope for the sampled editorial experience.

paths.description: Homepage and consent entry state; represents the primary news index, global navigation, search entry, privacy choice, responsive layout, performance, and security.
Politics/news section; represents section/listing templates. Audited for mobile reflow and template consistency.
Tour de France article; represents editorial detail pages, content hierarchy, metadata, no-JS resilience, and mobile reflow.
Search for “Bundestag”; represents the primary form journey and failure/recovery state. The endpoint returned a bare 403 in the audit browser.

findings.summary: A full-viewport consent/paywall choice obscures all content on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots show the consent layer occupying the entire viewport before interaction, with the underlying news content dimmed and inaccessible.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep essential content visible and move consent choices into a compact, dismissible, equally weighted interface that does not block reading.

findings.summary: The primary site search journey returns a bare 403 page in the audited browser.
findings.evidence: Submitting the site’s documented search target with q=Bundestag loaded https://suche.t-online.de/web?sr=1&q=Bundestag and returned only “403 Forbidden”.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the false-positive bot block for normal browser search traffic and provide an in-domain, progressively enhanced search results route.

findings.summary: The failed search state offers no explanation, retry, or route back to content.
findings.evidence: The search screenshot and DOM contain only “403 Forbidden”, with no navigation, recovery control, or retained query.
findings.suggestedFix: Render an actionable error state that preserves the query and offers retry, home, and support options.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 7.8s, interactive 12.9s, and performance 0.65; the independent trace measured LCP 5.42s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP element, reduce consent and script competition, and defer below-fold/third-party work.

findings.summary: The home load is heavy and critical delivery competes with consent and widget resources.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 124 requests, 2.02MB transferred, 50 scripts, and parser-inserted high-priority consent resources; LCP was 5.42–7.8s.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the critical chain, defer consent/widget bundles, set explicit resource priorities, and keep below-fold styles off the critical path.

findings.summary: Several links have no accessible name and search fields lack associated labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.87 and link-name failed for video and game links; DOM probes show search input labels are empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive link an accessible name and associate visible or screen-reader labels with each search input.

findings.summary: The page loads a large third-party and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 62 third-party requests and 1.12MB third-party transfer (56% of bytes); tracker evidence found 10 third-party origins and Google Tag Manager.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional third parties behind consent, remove low-value vendors, batch analytics, and self-host essential resources where feasible.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling collapses to an unbranded blank error.
findings.evidence: The representative search request returned only a bare 403 page, with no retry, navigation, or explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle 4xx/5xx and bot-challenge outcomes in the application shell with clear recovery actions.

findings.summary: The consent wall presents acceptance and a paid subscription as the prominent choices, without an equal reject option.
findings.evidence: Both desktop and mobile first-load screenshots show “ZUSTIMMEN” and “JETZT SICHERN” as the only primary actions; rejection requires entering the privacy manager.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer Accept and Reject All with equal prominence and keep the paid PUR offer separate from consent.

findings.summary: Third parties consume more than half of the initial transfer budget.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 1,123,471 of 2,017,478 transferred bytes to third parties, led by consent and engagement widgets.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce a third-party byte/request budget; defer or remove non-core widgets until explicit interaction.

findings.summary: The site imposes one dark palette instead of following the user’s light/dark preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots under default and prefers-color-scheme: dark are byte-identical; computed html color-scheme is normal, so the preference does not change the experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens so browser chrome and surfaces follow the user.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay is custom rather than a native dialog and has no clear light-dismiss path.
findings.evidence: The DOM reports one role=dialog but zero <dialog>, popover, or details elements; the first viewport has no visible close or reject action.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native <dialog> for the modal consent decision, provide explicit reject/close controls, restore focus, and use platform dismissal behavior where appropriate.

findings.summary: Navigation and consent chrome dominate the first viewport.
findings.evidence: The initial desktop screenshot is almost entirely consent UI, while the no-JS article screenshot devotes roughly 210px of a 493px viewport to two navigation rows and breadcrumbs before content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent header height, collapse secondary navigation, and remove the blocking consent wall so editorial content leads.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small and the search input lacks a visible focus indicator.
findings.evidence: The keyboard probe found 23 of the first 40 focusable elements under 24px in one dimension; the search input computed outline is none when focused.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24x24 CSS pixel targets (prefer 44x44 for primary touch controls) and a high-contrast :focus-visible ring for all controls.

findings.summary: Main-thread scripting adds noticeable blocking work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 280ms TBT; the trace captured two long tasks up to 88.53ms with 64.64ms trace TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks, schedule non-critical work by priority, and defer third-party widgets until needed.

findings.summary: Substantial unused JavaScript and CSS ships on the home page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 314KiB unused JavaScript and 49KiB unused CSS, including consent, GTM, game-widget, and core advertising code.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split non-editorial widgets, load third parties conditionally, and remove or scope unused CSS.

findings.summary: Breaking-news text does not meet WCAG minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.59:1 for magenta #e20074 text on #f5e198, below the required 4.5:1 for the sampled 18px bold label.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a darker text token or lighter background so normal text reaches at least 4.5:1.

findings.summary: Heading order is invalid and one key input has no visible focus ring.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse heading-order failed on an H3 teaser that skips hierarchy; the focus probe computed outline:none for the search input.
findings.suggestedFix: Use headings in a logical hierarchy and add consistent :focus-visible styles without removing the browser outline unless replaced.

findings.summary: Reflow works, but many targets remain undersized for touch and zoomed use.
findings.evidence: All three 360px layout probes had zero overflow, but the keyboard/geometry probe counted 23 of the first 40 focusable elements under 24px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target hit areas while preserving the successful fluid reflow.

findings.summary: Images are not consistently dimensioned or efficiently described.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 48/100 sampled images without width/height, 17 without srcset, and 52 legacy-format assets; Lighthouse also failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height (or aspect-ratio), responsive srcset/sizes, and modern formats where appropriate.

findings.summary: Transport is strong, but the CSP only controls framing and does not constrain scripts or other content.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, and CSP are present, but CSP is only “frame-ancestors self https://*.t-online.de” and Permissions-Policy is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP covering script-src and other resource types, and add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced policy coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: HSTS and CSP frame-ancestors protect transport/clickjacking, but Permissions-Policy is absent and CSP provides no script-src/Trusted Types defense.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive Permissions-Policy and expand CSP with script controls and require-trusted-types-for where compatible.

findings.summary: The public news experience is neither installable nor prepared for offline use.
findings.evidence: A manifest link exists, but the fetched manifest parsed as an empty object; the browser found zero service-worker registrations and zero caches.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a valid manifest and a service worker with an offline reading/fallback experience for recently viewed and shell content.

findings.summary: The first-load commercial/consent choice conflates privacy consent with a PUR subscription offer.
findings.evidence: The blocking dialog places “Kostenfrei mit Werbung” beside a €2.99/month PUR subscription while omitting an equally prominent reject path.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate privacy consent from subscription sales, state commitments clearly, and expose reversible consent controls at equal prominence.

findings.summary: Asset delivery leaves avoidable image waste.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 52/100 legacy-format images, 17 missing responsive srcset, 12 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and 48 missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where suitable, complete srcset/sizes coverage, lazy-load below-fold imagery, and reserve dimensions.

findings.summary: Unused and third-party work consumes substantial transfer and execution.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 314KiB unused JavaScript and HAR shows 50 script requests; 62 third-party requests account for 1.12MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load widgets and analytics, remove unused code, and deprioritize background fetches.

findings.summary: Navigation changes are abrupt despite the site being a multi-page reading experience.
findings.evidence: The rendered probe found no view-transition CSS or view-transition meta declaration on the home template, while navigation is through full document links.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } for cross-document article and section navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no visible reading progress or scroll-responsive chrome.
findings.evidence: The 18,000px home document and article template show fixed navigation/breadcrumbs, but the CSS probe found no scroll timeline and the sampled first viewport exposes no progress cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight CSS scroll progress indicator or scroll-state-aware header on long article and index pages.

findings.summary: The conventional sitemap endpoint does not return a sitemap and robots.txt declares none.
findings.evidence: GET /sitemap.xml returned a normal HTML page rather than XML sitemap data, while robots.txt contains no Sitemap directive; canonical URLs and HTTP 200 otherwise pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish an XML sitemap index and reference it from robots.txt.

findings.summary: The email sign-in field omits autocomplete metadata.
findings.evidence: The home form probe reports name=email with autocomplete empty; search explicitly uses autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=email and the appropriate username/current-password or passkey tokens in the full authentication flow.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No scroll-linked decorative animation was observed on the sampled news templates, so there is no scroll-event implementation to assess.
